newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany expresses solidarity with Rushdie.
newsitem.headline: Germany expresses solidarity with Rushdie.

text.p: Germany on Wednesday expressed its solidarity with British author Salman Rushdie after an Iranian foundation raised a reward for his assassination to $2.5 million.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Martin Erdmann said Germany had always rejected a 1989 religious edict imposed by Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini against Rushdie for alleged blasphemy against Islam in his novel "The Satanic Verses".
"Following the announcement today of increased bounty from a private, non-state, religious organisation, we reaffirm this position," Erdmann told reporters.
The Iranian daily Jomhuri Eslami reported on Wednesday that the 15th Khordad Foundation had raised its reward for Rushdie's death to $2.5 million from the original $2 million.
Erdmann also said Germany welcomed the fact that Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and other members of his government had distanced themselves from the announcement.
Since Khomeini issued the edict, or fatwa, Rushdie has been under 24-hour police protection, although he has in the past year been increasing the number of public appearances he makes.

"The European Union will tomorrow, on the eighth anniversary of the fatwa, reaffirm its solidarity with the British author in a declaration which is being agreed today and which will take account of the latest developments," Erdmann added.

Ties between Bonn and Iran have been strained in recent months over German prosecutors' accusations that Tehran ordered the 1992 gangland-style killings of three Kurdish dissidents in Berlin and a row over the whereabouts of an Iranian journalist.

In a letter published in several Western newspapers, the journalist -- Faraj Sarkuhi -- has alleged that he was detained and tortured by secret service agents in Iran late last year, when Tehran insists he was visiting Germany.
